facts.label: Who para vizinhos
facts.sub: Use who depois de pessoas para dizer o que elas fazem: people who live nearby, a man who walks dogs. Com people, use o verbo no plural.

facts.label: Que moram
facts.sub: Use who depois de pessoas: people who live nearby. Com people, o verbo fica no plural: live, help, work. Não adicione they depois de who.

facts.label: Verbo com s
facts.sub: Com uma pessoa, o verbo leva s: a man who walks dogs, the woman who lives upstairs. Com can, o verbo fica na base: who can help.

compare.ask: I know people who live nearby.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “as pessoas que moram perto” e o “que” liga a frase.

compare.us: Em inglês, para pessoas use who: people who live nearby. Com people, o verbo fica no plural. Com a man, o verbo leva s.

pages.title: The friendly street · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet Sunday morning in Cardiff. Small houses stand in a long line. Fern walks along her street with a coffee. She meets her neighbor Marco at his gate. They both love their friendly community. Fern asks about the new people nearby.

“Marco, do you know the people who live next door to you?” says Fern. “Yes, they are a family who moved here last spring.” says Marco. “Are they the ones who bring cookies to our street parties?” says Fern.
